name: Ethel Castilla
bio: Ethel Castilla (1861–1937) was an Australian poet, journalist and story writer, born at Kyneton, Victoria, and long resident in Melbourne. She was a founder of the Austral Salon, a meeting place for women writers and thinkers.
Her best-known poem, "An Australian Girl", first appeared in a Melbourne newspaper and gave its name to her collection The Australian Girl, and Other Verses (1900).

poems.title: An Australian Girl
poems.author: Ethel Castilla
poems.collection: A Victorian Anthology, 1837-1895, ed. Edmund Clarence Stedman
poems.text:
She has a beauty of her own,
A beauty of a paler tone
    Than English belles.
The Southern sun and Southern air
Have kissed her cheeks until they wear
The dainty tints that oft appear
    On rosy shells.

Her frank, clear eyes bespeak a mind
Old-world traditions fail to bind.
    She is not shy
Or bold, but simply self-possessed ;
Her independence adds a zest
Unto her speech, her piquant jest,
    Her quaint reply.

O'er classic volumes she will pore
With joy ; and some scholastic lore
    Will often gain.
In sports she bears away the bell,
Nor under music's siren spell
To dance divinely, flirt as well,
    Does she disdain.
